The general form is expcond ? valtrue : valfalse
- expcond is condition expression, for example val1 > val2, x == y etc.
- valtrue is the value when it's true
- valfalse is the value when it's false
This expression can be used like:
Which reduces the use of if(cond(val1, val2), valtrue, valfalse);.
For example: this expression verifies if time variable is even, then it's true (1), else false (0) using conditional ternary operator, assigned to q1.
The expression used above is equivalent to if(equal(time%2, 0), 1, 0) or if(time%2, 1, 0).

scenes.name: code implementation training #4 - two different bass reset with delay code and counting feature (Update 2024)

perFrameCode: timepeak = if(equal(time%0.1, 0),timepeak=timepeak+1/fps, timepeak); //the timepeak variable increases using the time variable in sync
timepeak2 = if(equal(time%0.1, 0),timepeak2=timepeak2+1/fps, timepeak2); //another one, but the same thing; both time sync now uses fps-independent algorithm. Thank you, Nitorami (martin)!
//timepeak = if(above(bass, 2),timepeak=0, timepeak); //reset the timepeak vaariable if the beat is below 2 (trigger algorithm) (commented this because not necessary)
bassdelay = timepeak>0.5; //declared the another variable with the simple condition

beatdelaytrigger = if(bassdelay, if(above(bass, 2), timepeak=0, timepeak), bleh); //another simple declaration, if the beat triggered with the delay above 0.5, it actually resets the timepeak variable to 0.
//Another Bass Trigger with Delay + count feature//
bassdelay2 = timepeak2>1; //same as the 2nd option, but the delay of 1 second.
beatdelaytrigger2 = if(bassdelay2, if(above(bass, 2), timepeak2=0, timepeak2), bleh);
count = if(bassdelay2, if(above(bass, 2), count=count+1, count), count); //it increments if it triggered the bass with the delay of 1 second.
count = if(count%8==0, count=0, count); //it resets to 0 if it passes to 8;
q1=timepeak; //we carry this variable to custom shapes, waves etc.
